subject: Recap: Technical trial plan & owners — ClearHealth
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Ortiz <maya@clearhealth.com>, Tomas Alvarez <tomas@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Technical trial plan & owners — ClearHealth

Hi Maya / Tomas —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Quick written recap and a proposed technical trial plan so we can lock owners and dates into the MAP. I attached the current MAP draft and a short latency/cost spec.

High-level goal: validate model shortlist on ClearHealth test set and demonstrate latency & unit-cost targets for a production-like integration. Target close for the MAP milestone: 2026-10-15 (open to adjustment if you surface major blockers).

Proposed milestones and owners (please confirm):
- Milestone A — Test harness & dataset delivery (owner: ClearHealth / Tomas) — Due: 2026-09-30
  - Deliver: 5k representative prompts + expected output checks, schema for PII redaction, sample queries.
- Milestone B — Latency & cost baseline runs (owner: Redwood / Laura) — Due: 2026-10-07
  - Run: 3 model variants across 1k warm and 1k cold queries, collect p50/p95/p99 latencies and tokenized cost.
- Milestone C — Quality parity pass (owner: ClearHealth / Maya + Redwood ML lead) — Due: 2026-10-12
  - Acceptance: automated QA pass + manual spot-checks on 200 outputs.
- Milestone D — Final readout & signoff (Owners: Sales + Platform) — Target: 2026-10-15

Initial benchmark success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 300 ms (production-like infra)
- Cost: token cost target <= $0.60 per 1k input+output tokens (OP-ex estimate)
- Quality: automated BLEU/ROUGE-style pass rate >= 90% on core intent set; manual spot-check score >= 4/5

Model shortlist for trial (first pass):
- rw-3b-q8 (low-cost, quantized)
- rw-7b-fp16 (higher quality, mid-cost)
- open-13b-q4 (control for larger model behavior)

Dependencies / blockers to call out:
- ClearHealth to provide test data + data access credentials (VPN / S3)
- SOC2 evidence request in parallel (affects dedicated infra options)
- If you want on-prem/air-gapped runs, that will shift timeline by ~2-3 weeks

Ask from ClearHealth: please confirm owners and any additional acceptance criteria by EOD Monday (2026-09-20).

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-v0.2.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)], [Attachment: latency-benchmark-specs.pdf (pdf, 210 KB)]

Thanks — I’ll slot follow-ups in based on confirmations.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Maya Ortiz <maya@clearhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Tomas Alvarez <tomas@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Technical trial plan & owners — ClearHealth

Thanks Jasmine — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. Quick confirmations from our side:

- Owners: Tomas will own dataset delivery (confirmed). I will own the quality review/acceptance (Milestone C).
- Dates: 2026-09-30 for dataset is tight but achievable — we’ll prioritize a 5k sample by then and complete the broader dump later.
- Acceptance: add one additional criterion — p95 <= 120 ms for interactive flows (where latency is most visible). If the p95 bound is not met, we want a mitigation plan from Redwood (quantization or routing) in the final readout.

One more ask: can Redwood provide a short doc detailing the exact environment used for the benchmark (GPU type / tuning) so we can evaluate parity with our infra?

I’ll email Tomas to confirm the sample delivery plan separately.

Best,
Maya Ortiz
Head of Product Integrations | ClearHealth
maya@clearhealth.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Ortiz <maya@clearhealth.com>, Tomas Alvarez <tomas@clearhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Technical trial plan & owners — ClearHealth

Rishi / Laura — forwarding Maya's confirmation and the two asks (notably the tighter p95 target and request for environment details). Can you please: 

1) Confirm which infra/profile we will run the trial on and provide a 1-paragraph environment spec (GPU, memory, runtime flags, quantization profile).
2) Confirm the exact benchmark scripts we’ll run (we should include warm vs cold, batch sizes, concurrency).
3) Commit to owners for run scheduling and reporting (who will do the runs and who will prepare the readout slide).
4) If the p95 <= 120 ms target looks infeasible on the current shortlist, propose a fallback model or routing policy we can test during the trial.

Suggested quick acceptance criteria (update based on Rishi feedback):
- Latency: p95 <= 120 ms (interactive), p99 <= 300 ms
- Cost: <= $0.60 per 1k tokens (goal), fallback acceptable up to $0.85 for higher-quality model if latency is in-range
- Quality: automated pass >=90% on intents + manual spot-check >= 4/5

Can you take the owner commitments and reply by EOD today? I’ll hold off scheduling the run until we have infra confirmation.

— Jasmine

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Ortiz <maya@clearhealth.com>, Tomas Alvarez <tomas@clearhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Technical trial plan & owners — ClearHealth

Thanks — I can take ownership of the benchmark runs and readout. Quick notes and commitments from the infra/bench perspective: 

- Environment (will document and share link): AWS p4d instance (8x A100 40GB) for fp16 runs; a 4xA10G pool for quantized runs. Runtime: Redwood Inference serving runtime v2.3 with continuous batching enabled, kernel tuning as per default profile.
- Quantization: rw-3b-q8 and open-13b-q4 will be tested with q4/q8 profiles; rw-7b-fp16 as float baseline.
- Concurrency / batch: will run at concurrency 8 and 32 to capture interactive vs throughput behavior; warm runs = 500 queries after a 100-query warmup.
- Acceptance feasibility: p95 <= 120 ms is achievable on rw-3b-q8 in the A10G pool with batching/concurrency tuned (we’ll validate). rw-7b-fp16 will likely hit p95 ~= 200 ms; open-13b-q4 likely higher. If Interactive p95 fails for larger models, we’ll test selective routing to rw-3b-q8 for interactive flows and larger models for async batch tasks.
- Cost estimate (rough): rw-3b-q8: ~$0.25 per 1k tokens; rw-7b-fp16: ~$0.55 per 1k tokens; open-13b-q4: ~$0.95 per 1k tokens. Detailed token accounting attached.

I’m attaching the latency benchmark spec with exact scripts and expected outputs. I’ll schedule the runs next Tue/Wed (2026-09-22 / 23) — will share raw logs + summarized slide deck by 2026-10-07.

Attachments: [Attachment: latency-benchmark-specs.pdf (pdf, 210 KB)]

— Rishi
Lead, Platform Performance | Redwood Inference
